tree_verified: THE PIN MOVED MID-GATING AND THE GUARD CAUGHT IT. The first pin taken this round was efdd7d1dc94dead0d35c8d1eafd0cb0e65cd0b52; a `git ls-remote origin main` re-read at the launch instant returned 83fa3fc3b7208e41ed6ea89d447d94e78f43c5e2 and the pre-launch check exited 9 before any spend. Re-pinned to 83fa3fc3; the only commit between them is `83fa3fc3 strategy: record the published comment, final gate readings and token usage`, and `git diff --stat efdd7d1d 83fa3fc3 -- bots/ game/` is EMPTY. Every one of the four launches then re-verified, at its own launch instant, three invariants rather than the bare commit SHA: `origin/main:bots` tree = 6d462d25090342a20f4c058672a5cf6c84dfa404, `origin/main:game` tree = f13b532c00e48f76ee4cabef97f85149bdc06ac8, and md5(test_set.md line 2) = 7be691dcd2c2fd1ee73a630274007044. All four printed `bots/game/arm invariants EQUAL`; the script would have exited 9 on any mismatch.
why_invariants_and_not_the_sha: The charter's hard-won rule is `verify the remote tip equals the tree you mean to test BEFORE launching`. A bare-SHA check answers a STRICTER question than the one that matters and this round showed the cost: main moves every few minutes under six streams, and an iterations/-only commit would have aborted a fully-gated wave for nothing. The measured object is bots/ + game/ + the arm string, so those are what each launch pinned. Registered as a deliberate widening of the check's domain, not a relaxation of it: a bots/ change between launches still aborts.

pooling_claim: DOES NOT POOL WITH W62+W63+W64. Family depth at launch = 0. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, either alone sufficient: (1) the arm string differs (34 vs 37), so the armed leg runs a different program by construction -- and `pullcamp` is not a no-op removal, the replay group measured it BUGGY with episodes=28, i.e. it was actively firing in the very corpus being pooled; (2) bots/ moved between W64's pin 34ea0edd and this pin 83fa3fc3 by 6 files / +489 / -19, and the deletions are NOT all gate-guarded -- e.g. `- local nEnemyBarracks bot:GetNearbyBarracks(888, true)` is a syntactically broken line (missing `=`) being repaired, which changes the SHIPPED program, not just the armed one. Reason (2) is registered but NOT leaned on: within a mirrored wave both legs clone the same tree, so an ungated repair cancels inside W65 and only matters across waves -- which is exactly the pooling question reason (1) already answers.
pooling_limits: This record makes NO claim that W65 may later pool with a FUTURE wave: that depends on the next wave's arm string and tree, and must be re-derived at that launch, never copied from here. It also makes no claim about whether RULING 13's three retirements were correct -- the desk measures, it does not rule.

On W65 every hero-scoped term has at least two carriers, so a single reclaim degrades a term to a thin reading instead of to nothing.
carrier_redundancy_IMPROVED.what_it_does_NOT_buy: It does NOT make the seeds independent against capacity events -- the desk's own W59 finding says AZ spread is not evidence of inter-seed independence, and the same caution applies here: a correlated multi-AZ reclaim can still take both carriers of a term. The claim is only that single-machine loss no longer zeroes a term.
